task: foot scale check vs master sheet (report only, nothing fixed)
pass_rule: a foot fails if its length or width differs by more than 1 px from master-sheet proportions scaled to the same head height (crown-chin) in the measured image (turn frames also given in rig display px)

master_sheet.not_used: reference/grok_build/.../Shadowveil_Interactive_Master_Sheet.html "Original anatomy turnaround" (asset c785b213cc7bbdb864eb): a different-looking character (skin, face), so not used as her proportions

sources.live_body: browser rest renders of rig/index.html?view=<v> (render/out2/<v>_live/rest.png); the rest alpha equals views/<v>/base.png
sources.staged_body: body_tools/work/hairless_division_staged/<v>/hairless_<v>.png (current, line-tone-snapped files). The rig render with ?hairless=1 came out pixel-identical to the live render (hair still drawn although RigHairless.on=true), so it cannot stand in for the staged body; its feet = live feet = staged feet (0 alpha px differ in the feet band)

turn_frames.note: the driver shows these authored frames during the turn (the rig is not composited at these angles), so the frames are what she looks like at each angle

sources.line_colour_note: masks are alpha (rig) / non-white (master) / non-blue-key (frames), so the snapped line tones (apose 12,11,29; tpose 12,12,29; left 12,10,28; right 11,11,28; back 12,12,31) do not move the outline; the results are unchanged after the snap

rendering.md5_note: the brief said live rig/index.html starts with 0ce6fecc; at check time (02:0x PT) the live file is 00892ccb..., so the tree was re-copied and rendered against 00892ccb (served md5 == live md5, checked inside every page before rendering). Renders made against the earlier 0ce6fecc copy were discarded.
rendering.ports: no TCP port used: 8772 and 8774 were LISTENING (another agent's python3 servers; 8773 was also busy earlier) and were left alone; files are served to the page with Playwright request routing at http://svfoot.invalid/ (no 8765/8766)
rendering.poses: rest, ankle+-1, toe+-1, knee+-1, hip+-1, knee/ankle combos, all+1, all-1 (both legs, every other param at default)
rendering.posed_method: each posed render is inverse-warped by that foot's bone matrix R._BM[foot_X] into the rest foot frame, then measured with the same rule as rest (ankle row pinned to rest). mean_outline_offset_px = XOR px of the rigid foot below the ankle blend / rest outline length

definitions.head: crown (topmost outline px; on haired images the top of the bun because the skull top under the bun cannot be seen) to chin (front: chin line on the midline; profile: lowest chin underside; 3/4: picked on zoom; back views: transferred from the matching front image by sole offset x height ratio). Staged (hairless) images are also compared with the live head of the same view (*_vs_live_head) because their own crown is the cranium, which is lower than the haired crown
definitions.forearm: rig images: elbow = parts.json joints.elbow_X.pivot, length = perpendicular distance to the wrist_line_X.json line. Master and frames: elbow crease/olecranon mark centre to the wrist break, picked on zoom (see per-image landmarks)
definitions.foot_front_back: length = vertical extent from the ankle row (narrowest leg row in [sole-0.10H, sole-0.035H]) to the lowest outline px (a soft proxy: the heel-toe axis points at the camera; length_range is the ankle plateau); width = widest horizontal run of the foot (ball)
definitions.foot_profile_3q: length = heel-to-toe-tip chord (toe = foremost outline px in the lowest 22% of the foot; heel = rearmost px in the lowest 45% (profile) or below the top 20% (3/4)); width = outline extent perpendicular to the chord at 72% from the heel (ball). Profile width is foot thickness and is not comparable when the far foot overlaps
definitions.sides: front views: image-left = her R; back views: image-left = her L; left view = her L (near), right = her R; f033 near L, f191 near R, f087 near L, f131 near R

resolution_caveat: the master JPG has about 1.7 rig px per master px (head 150-160 px vs 265-281 px on the rig), so a 1 px tolerance is finer than the master can resolve; delta_interval_px gives the +-1 px (master) / +-0.5-1 px (image) uncertainty. "FAIL robust" = the whole interval lies beyond 1 px
